M8.L1.title: Describe two-dimensional shapes based on attributes.

M8.L2.title: Build, identify, and analyze two-dimensional shapes with specified attributes.

M8.L3.title: Use attributes to draw different polygons including triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, and hexagons.

M8.L4.title: Use attributes to identify and draw different quadrilaterals including rectangles, rhombuses, parallelograms, and trapezoids.

M8.L5.title: Classify and sort three-dimensional shapes by their attributes.

M8.L6.title: Combine shapes to create a composite shape; create a new shape from composite shapes.

M8.L7.title: Interpret equal shares in composite shapes as halves, thirds, and fourths.

M8.L8.title: Interpret equal shares in composite shapes as halves, thirds, and fourths.

M8.L9.title: Partition circles and rectangles into equal parts, and describe those parts as halves, thirds, or fourths.

M8.L10.title: Partition circles and rectangles into equal parts, and describe those parts as halves, fourths, and eighths.

M8.L11.title: Use concrete models to count fractional parts beyond one whole.

M8.L12.title: Construct a paper clock by partitioning a circle into halves and quarters, and tell time to the half hour or quarter hour.

M8.L13.title: Tell time to the nearest five minutes.

M8.L14.title: Tell time to the nearest five minutes; relate a.m. and p.m. to time of day.

M8.L15.title: Relate skip counting by fives on the clock and telling time to a continuous measurement model, the number line.

M8.L16.title: Count by fives and ones on the number line as a strategy to tell time to the nearest minute on the clock.
